thread:
deploy-bot: :rotating_light: Canary cutover started for `prompt-route-v3` -> 5% traffic. Canary group: eu-west-1, canary-id=canary-83. Rolling strategy: linear. Will post status updates.

maya: seeing a spike in 502/504 from the new endpoint almost immediately. dashboards show increased p50/p95 for prompt endpoint in eu-west. Example trace:
```
ERROR 2026-03-15T14:12:05Z prompt-router: upstream: timeout after 2.5s id=xyz-1234 status=504
stack: router::handle_request -> model_proxy::call -> timeout
```

eli: @maya can you confirm whether it's model backend timing out or the routing layer? Also if cached routes are involved.

maya: looks like routing layer is returning 504s before model backend logs any heavy work. latency jumps at the router (connection resets) and the new endpoint's health probes show occasional 500s. Attaching a small curl repro:
```
curl -v 'https://api.redwood.ai/prompt/v3/complete' -H 'Authorization: Bearer xxxxx' -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'
* TCP_NODELAY set
< HTTP/1.1 504 Gateway Timeout
```

oncall-bot: PAGER: paging oncall (reason: increased 5xx rate for prompt-route-v3 canary) -> paged: eli

eli: I'm paged, taking lead. @sara please prepare to flip the feature flag if we confirm it's routing regressions. @ops standby for rollback of canary.

sara: running flag toggle: POST to /feature-flags/prompt_route_v3 -> payload {"enabled": false, "actor":"sara"}
Response: {"status":"ok","new_state":"off","ts":"2026-03-15T14:14:20Z"}

sara: :white_check_mark: feature flag prompt_route_v3 -> OFF (propagation to edge should be ~30s)

ops: starting traffic reroute: updating route table to send canary traffic back to prompt-route-v2. Command used:
```
redwoodctl routing patch --route prompt-route --set-default=prompt-v2
```

infra-bot: system: CDN cache purge queued for prefix `/v3/prompt/*` (request id purge-5591)

maya: after FF off + route patch, 5xxs dropped to baseline in eu-west within ~45s. We still see a handful of failing sessions due to cached routes (some clients hit older edge nodes). Purge should handle it.

customer-success: any estimate on impacted customers? need to notify support for potentially affected accounts.

maya: quick impact estimate: ~0.18% of overall requests during the 7m window, concentrated in eu-west and mostly low-traffic PLG apps. No major enterprise customers showed errors in our logs, but 3 customer IDs had sustained errors for >1m. I'll export the list to #support.

arjun: please add a postmortem checklist item: verify canary's health checks are adequate for this routing change and add an early abort rule if 5xx rate > 0.5% in first 2m.

eli: agreed. For now mitigation steps:
- flag off (sara) :white_check_mark:
- route default -> v2 (ops) :white_check_mark:
- cdn purge (infra-bot) :white_check_mark:
- monitor for residual errors (maya)

oncall-bot: Incident severity: SEV2 -> paging stopped. Handoff: eli remains owner for one hour, then hand to next oncall if all stable.

sara: logged the action in deploy logs: `ff_toggle prompt_route_v3 off by sara` (id toggle-20260315-14:14)

ops: canary rollback recorded: canary-83 -> rolled back at 2026-03-15T14:15:12Z. No further rollouts until postmortem.

maya: customers notified in #support: 3 customers flagged for follow-up, CS to reach out with timeline. Will attach logs and sample request IDs.

eli: assigning postmortem to @maya and @arjun. Tasks:
- collect timing + traces for canary window
- review health checks and readiness probes for prompt-route-v3
- add automatic abort rule for routing-level 5xx spikes
- decide whether to reattempt with smaller canary or additional checks

customer-success: acknowledged, will coordinate outreach and share any customer replies in this thread.

ops: creating follow-up ticket (TICKET-4451) for canary rollout automation improvements and FF kill switch runbook updates.

maya: final status: system metrics back to baseline, no active pager. keeping watch for 30m, will add logs to incident folder.

eli: thanks team. immediate ops done. leaving incident open for postmortem creation. :thumbsup:
